ARCH-TAB-003.title: Tabernacle Holy Place
ARCH-TAB-003.note: Looking west: seven-lamp stand south/left, table north/right, incense altar before one continuous veil. Twelve visible flat cakes form two rows of six; flat shape and row layout are selected interpretations of the KJV provision. Four gold inner-veil pillars have silver bases. Furniture spacing, fittings and woven guardian anatomy are reconstructed. Human-headed winged-sphinx anatomy is a selected ancient Near Eastern interpretation; the KJV does not specify that detailed anatomy.
ARCH-TAB-003.alt: Tabernacle Holy Place. Reconstructed Wilderness setting; chronology not fixed.

ARCH-FIR-007.note: Kings-based Sea with two rows of knops beneath the rim; Chronicles instead describes ox-like decoration. Kings gives 2000 baths and Chronicles 3000; no modern capacity is certified.

ARCH-ZER-001.title: Zerubbabel: rebuilding at the foundation
ARCH-ZER-001.note: Foundation-stage reconstruction: Ezra places the working altar before the Temple foundation and names stone, carpenters and cedar. The rough-stone altar applies Exodus 20’s law as a selected deduction; Ezra does not supply its complete form. Work arrangements and unfinished foundation layout are interpreted. Ezra 6’s decree gives height 60 and breadth 60, not length or a surveyed as-built floor plan.
ARCH-ZER-001.alt: Zerubbabel: rebuilding at the foundation. Reconstructed Persian-period reconstruction; Ezra 3 foundation stage.

ARCH-HER-002.title: Herodian sanctuary: east front
ARCH-HER-002.note: Reconstructed from ancient descriptions, not a surviving elevation. This model selects Middot where its dimensions differ from Josephus; the sources are not averaged. Open outer portal selects Middot 40 by 20, not Josephus 70 by 25; exact dimensions are controlled by source notes, not perspective measurement. Gilding applies to principal east front with white portions retained after Josephus; selected Middot portal differs from Josephus.
ARCH-HER-002.alt: Herodian sanctuary: east front. Reconstructed First-century pre-AD 70 reconstruction.

ARCH-HER-006.title: Temple Mount: southern approach
ARCH-HER-006.note: Archaeology-informed southern approach with reconstructed superstructure. Surviving masonry has several phases; present upper courses are not all Herodian. Gate elevations, upper windows, baths, stoa completion and steps are reconstructed. Acts 21’s fortress access is not identified with this southern stair.
ARCH-HER-006.alt: Temple Mount: southern approach. Reconstructed First-century pre-AD 70 approach reconstruction.

ARCH-CTX-001.title: Magdala: first-century synagogue comparison
ARCH-CTX-001.period: Early Roman Magdala; selected reconstruction of the synagogue’s last reported phase
ARCH-CTX-001.note: Magdala archaeological comparison, not Nazareth or proof Jesus used this building. The roof is removed for teaching. Six columns complete Netzer’s proposed reconstruction from fragments; they are not six recovered complete shafts. Benches/corridor, partial mosaic and fresco evidence inform the room. The carved four-footed stone’s function is proposed; far feet and the near bench are partly obscured. IAA’s 2013 preliminary report mentions a 43 CE coin in mosaic bedding; the picture is not certified as an AD 30 interior.
ARCH-CTX-001.alt: Magdala: first-century synagogue comparison. Reconstructed Early Roman Magdala; selected reconstruction of the synagogue’s last reported phase.

ARCH-CTX-002.title: Bethesda: two pools and five porches

Ritual-bath/reserve functions and portico phasing remain debated. Roofs, surrounding buildings, water level, depths and exact step counts are not certified.
ARCH-CTX-002.alt: Bethesda: two pools and five porches. Reconstructed First-century textual and archaeological reconstruction.

WORLD-TRV-004.alt: Roadside inn and animal court. First-century southern-Levant accommodation comparison. Study reconstruction.

sources.t: IAA Horbat Ashun early Roman domestic/courtyard comparison

WORLD-OBJ-003.title: Scrolls, jars and writing materials
WORLD-OBJ-003.period: Late Second Temple Judaea, first century BC-first century AD
WORLD-OBJ-003.note: Ancient material comparison, not an original KJV manuscript or a named biblical scroll. Text is rolled or hidden; no invented ancient-language passage is presented. Grouping, relative sizes, wraps and reed-pen completion are inferred; this is not one recovered assemblage.
WORLD-OBJ-003.alt: Scrolls, jars and writing materials. Late Second Temple Judaea, first century BC-first century AD. Study reconstruction.

sources.t: IAA objects exhibited by Library of Congress: scroll materials
IAA objects exhibited by Library of Congress: writing materials

WORLD-OBJ-004.title: Roman and Jewish small coin comparison
WORLD-OBJ-004.note: Interpretive coin motif study, not a numismatic facsimile or proof of the exact Gospel tribute coin. Historic legends are intentionally unrepresented; precise dies, wear and relative size are not certified. Historic coin legends are intentionally omitted from this enlarged motif study, not evidence of uninscribed mint designs. Portrait, die detail, wear and relative size are interpretive.
WORLD-OBJ-004.alt: Roman and Jewish small coin comparison. Selected first-century coin types. Study reconstruction.

sources.t: Getty collection: Tiberius denarius comparison, AD14-37
Ashmolean Roman Provincial Coinage I, 4981: Agrippa I

WORLD-OBJ-005.title: Balance and stone weights

WORLD-OBJ-005.alt: Balance and stone weights. Iron Age southern-Levant material comparison. Study reconstruction.
